Headline: Promoter Shares of Asian Life Insurance Company and Lumbini Bikas Bank in Auction From Today
Full Content:
The existing promoter of
Asian Life Insurance Company Limited (ALICL)
is auctioning the company's promoter shares. 100,000 shares are being auctioned from today, i.e. Bhadra 22, 2079.
100,000 units promoter shares of ALICL are being auctioned. The auction is first open to existing promoters for 15 days from the day of the official notice i.e Bhadra 22 (today). If not bought by existing promoters, the public and other institutions/ companies will then be eligible to bid for the shares.
ALICL has a total of 15,239,010 units promoter shares, amounting to 60% of the company's shareholding.

Headline: 25.39 Lakh Additional Share Supply of Asian Life Insurance (ALICL) to Enter Secondary Market, Company Converted Promoter Shares
Full Content:
Asian Life Insurance Company Limited (ALICL)
has made changes to its shareholding ratio by converting a portion of promoter shares to ordinary shares.
Previously, the promoter to the public shareholding ratio of the company was 70:30. As of writing, the paid-up capital of the company is Rs 2,539,835,000. Thus, promoters own 70,% i.e. Rs. 152.38 crores of the paid-up capital, and the public shareholders own 30%, i.e. Rs. 101.59 crores.
The 12th AGM of the company endorsed the conversion of shareholding ratio from 70: 30 to 60: 40 by converting a portion of the promoter shares to ordinary shares. Thus, 25.39 lakh promoter shares were converted to ordinary shares. This will mean an additional supply of the same quantity of shares that will be traded in the secondary market as ordinary shares.

Headline: Asian Life Insurance Converting Promoter Shares to Change Shareholding Ratio
Full Content:
Asian Life Insurance Company Limited
has published a notice regarding the conversion of share structure from 70: 30 to 60: 40.
The 12th AGM of the company endorsed the conversion of shareholding ratio from 70: 30 to 60: 40 by converting a portion of the promoter shares to ordinary shares.
Promoters unwilling to convert their shares can submit a declaration at the company's central office in Maitidevi, Kathmandu within 7 days of the unveiling of this notice.
If such declaration letter is not received by the aforementioned timeframe, the shares will be automatically converted.

Headline: This Is the Red List of 51 Companies That Are Overvalued, According to SEBON
Full Content:
The Securities Board of Nepal has unveiled a list of 51 companies trading in NEPSE to better inform investors about their real financial picture.
The list contains the closing price of the companies as of Shrawan 12, 2073, when the NEPSE index was at 1,881.45. Alongside is a list that has the closing price of the respective companies as of Baisakh 30, 2077. The NEPSE index closed at 1,221.31 that day. On the right, the list has the closing price of the same companies yesterday, i.e. Jestha 31, 2078, when the index closed at 3,025.83.
The regulatory board prepared this list based on the abnormality in percentage gain of the stock price of such companies in relation to their current financial health. These are stocks that have gained more than 300% in recent times, have a P/E ratio higher than 100, and various other factors.
With this, the board has urged investors to invest not on rumor or stock tips, but only after analyzing the financials of the scrips. Nonetheless, the board has thanked investors for utilizing the online platform during the pandemic that made the recent surge in intraday activity possible. The board has stated that the capital market will endure only as high as the confidence among investors. As such, SEBON has requested investors to maintain stability by taking informed financial decisions.

Headline: NIC Asia Bank auctioning Promoter Shares of 4 Companies from Today
Full Content:
NIC Asia Bank Limited is auctioning the promoter shares of four companies. The auctioning has already opened from today, i.e. Poush 27. It will conclude on 5th Magh.
The bank is auctioning 2,02,560 units promoter share of Citizen Investment Trust (CIT) and 1,02,866 units promoter share of National Life Insurance Company Limited (NLICL).
Similarly, it is auctioning 1,89,664 units of promoter shares of Surya Life Insurance Company (SLICL) and 1,28,790 units of promoter shares of Asian Life Insurance Company (ALICL).
Only banks, financial institutions, and insurance companies are allowed to bid for the auction of Citizen Investment Trust's shares. Meanwhile, all eligible investors can bid for the auction of promoter shares of other companies.
While the minimum bid quantity is 100 units for all the auctions, there is no upper limit. Although bidders can bid for the entirety of the issue, they are required to abide by Nepal Rastra Bank's rule to not exceed the specified quantity of shares per entity. Meanwhile, any quantity in between should be divisible by 10.
The minimum bid rate for CIT's shares is Rs. 1,530 while that for NLICL's shares is Rs. 508. Similarly, the minimum bid rate for ALICL and SLICL's auction is Rs. 433 and Rs. 350 respectively.
NIC Asia Capital is the auction manager.
